title: Reading and writing workload groups: API, SDKs, Terraform, MCP

prose.text: The API supports list, get, create, update and delete; clients differ in what they expose and in how lookup by name works.

prose.label: Listing and finding one by name.
prose.text: {{list-paging}} {{no-name-filter}} {{go-getbyname-client-side}} Because the Go SDK walks every page for a name lookup, the general page-size and truncation hazards in [[shared.sdk-go.list-pagination]] apply to it.

prose.label: Terraform.
prose.text: {{tf-import}} {{tf-activation-guard}} The environment gate and what activation publishes are in [[zia.terraform.activation]]. {{console-activation}}
For what goes in `expressionJson` and which fields are writable in which tool, see [[zia.workload-groups.expressions]].

checks.do: Whether a name that MCP reports as not found sits on a later page, by requesting further pages explicitly.
Whether the count matches the console when a name is not found, since the Go lookup walks every page.

crud-endpoints.statement: The ZIA API exposes list and create on `/workloadGroups`, and get, update (PUT) and delete on `/workloadGroups/{workloadGroupId}`; the Go SDK uses the endpoint `/zia/api/v1/workloadGroups`.

Workload Group Resource Add Workload Group
Workload Group Resource Get Workload Group By ID
Workload Group Resource Update Workload Group
Workload Group Resource Delete Workload Group

postman-get-all-only.statement: The OneAPI Postman collection holds only a "Workload Groups - Get all" request, a GET on `{{ZIABaseUrl}}/workloadGroups`; it is not a source for the write schema.

list-paging.statement: Listing takes `page` and `pageSize`; the contract states a default page size of 250 and a maximum of 1,000, and the Python SDK documents the same.

expect.name: pageSize
expect.description: Specifies the page size. The default size is 250 and the maximum size is 1,000.

quotes: The default size is 250, but the maximum size is 1000.

no-name-filter.statement: The list endpoint has no server-side name filter: the contract defines only `page` and `pageSize`, and the MCP workflow says to filter by name client-side.

quotes: The ZIA list endpoint does **not** support a server-side `name` filter

go-getbyname-client-side.statement: The Go SDK's `GetByName` reads every page and compares names with `strings.EqualFold`, so a lookup by name is client-side and case-insensitive.

mcp-jmespath-query.statement: The MCP list tool takes only `page` and `page_size`; the bridge adds an optional JMESPath `query` applied to the results after the API call.

quotes: page: Annotated[Optional[int], Field(default=None, description="Page number (1-based).")] = None
page_size: Annotated[Optional[int], Field(default=None, description="Items per page.")] = None
"Optional JMESPath expression applied to the results after the API "

mcp-query-one-page.statement: A name lookup through the MCP `query` therefore filters only the page the API call returned, not the whole tenant, unless the caller pages through the results.
mcp-query-one-page.conditions: Derived from the tool passing only page and page_size to the API and the bridge applying query after the call; no source tests a name lookup across pages.

mcp-read-only.statement: The MCP server exposes workload groups read-only; authoring them is left to the ZIA console.

quotes: Workload group authoring (with its expression DSL) is intentionally left to the ZIA UI.

tf-import.statement: The Terraform `zia_workload_groups` resource imports by numeric ID or, if the argument is not numeric, by name through `GetByName`; it exposes `group_id` as a computed alias for the ID.

tf-activation-guard.statement: Create, update and delete of the Terraform resource trigger activation only when `ZIA_ACTIVATION` is set to a truthy value.

quotes: // Check if ZIA_ACTIVATION is set to a truthy value before triggering activation

field-types.statement: In the API contract, `lastModifiedBy` is a reference object with `id`, `name` (read-only) and optional `extensions`, and `lastModifiedTime` is an integer timestamp.

expect.description: Timestamp when the workload group was last modified

console-activation.statement: In the console, a saved workload group change must be activated.

quotes: Click Save and activate the change.

name-required-and-epoch.title: Whether name is required on create and the unit of lastModifiedTime
name-required-and-epoch.blocks: stating validation behavior and converting the timestamp
name-required-and-epoch.detail: Unverified legacy statement: "`name` ... Required on create (SDK enforces via `add_group`)" and "`last_modified_time` int (epoch)". The contract does not mark name required and the Python add_group docs only describe it as the name; the timestamp unit is not stated.
